To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the asymptotic behavior in the sense of free cumulantics of the Jucys– Murphy operators is given by the normalized characters of the representation of S q, the appropriate rescaling being given by q −1 2, and that the second order asymptotics of the characters evaluated on cycles is given by Kerov polynomials.

1) the free cumulant of a Jucys– Murphy element is the normalized character of the appropriate representation; 2) the normalized character of an irreducible representation of the symmetric or the unitary group can be expressed in terms of the transition measure associated to the Young diagram of the corresponding representation; and 3) the transition measure associated a Young diagram can be expressed in the form of the free cumulant of the corresponding Jucys– Murphys element.

the free cumulant of a Young diagram of size n and the normalized character of a representation of S q evaluated on a cycle of length k are asymptotically equivalent to the same function evaluated on a Young diagram of the size n − 1 and the representation of the group S q − 1, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
asymptotic expansions of the characters of representations of the symmetric groups.
the asymptotic behavior (as q → ∞) of characters of irreducible representations of symmetric groups S q evaluated on the cycle structure of permutations.
the asymptotic analysis of representations of the group S q.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our results provide an explicit formula for the second order asymptotics of characters of the symmetric group evaluated on cycles.
the free cumulant generating functions of transition measures are asymptotic expansions of the normalized characters of representations of the corresponding symmetric group.
the second order asymptotics of free cumulats and Kerov polynomials is governed by the second order term of the asymptotics of characters of symmetric groups evaluated on cycles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the asymptotic behavior (as q → ∞) of characters evaluated on a cycle is governed by the asymptotic behavior as q → ∞ of free cumulats evaluated at the corresponding Jucys– Murphy element.
the second order asymptotics for the free cumulats and for the Kerov polynomials can be obtained by a simple application of a well known formula of Littlewood and Richardson.
we provide a free probability interpretation of Kerov’s polynomials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the free cumulantics are asymptotically given by the characters of representations of S q. This is the free analog of the classical result of Kerov and Vershik [KV].
the asymptotic expansion in terms of free probabilities of a large class of symmetric group characters can be computed explicitly.

the asymptotics of characters of representations of S q can be expressed in terms of the transition measure associated to a Young diagram, which is a probability measure on the space of infinite Young diagrams.
